title: Genome editing in archaeal viruses and endogenous viral protein purification
protocol: Eliminate the original virus while allowing the mutant virus to propagate.
Select a 39- to 45-bp protospacer within the region of interest in the virus genome.
Ensure the selected protospacer fulfills specified criteria.
Screen the region of interest in the virus genome for a non-redundant protospacer flanked by a 5′-GTN-3′ PAM compatible with type I-D CRISPR-Cas systems.
Assemble the spacer DNA element using two ssDNA oligonucleotides complementary to each strand of the selected protospacer.
Include 3-nt 5′-overhanging sequences in each ssDNA oligonucleotide for cloning purposes.
Clone the final spacer DNA element between type subtype I-D repeats found in pGE2.
Insert donor DNA into the multiple cloning site of pGE2, located between PaeI and XhoI restriction sites.
Ensure transcriptional start site (TSS) initiates transcription from an arabinose promoter (ara-box), B recognition element (BRE), and TATA-box for the mini-CRISPR-array in pGE2.
Remove or disrupt the protospacer sequence in the desired mutant virus.
Design and order ssDNA oligos complementary to the selected protospacer.
Add equal volumes of the two ssDNA oligos (10 μM stocks) to a microcentrifuge tube.
Vortex the mixture to mix thoroughly.
Incubate the mixture at 95°C for 10 min in a heat block.
Allow the mixture to cool gradually to room temperature.
Store the resulting dsDNA spacer element at -20°C until needed.
Clone the dsDNA spacer element into a linearized (FD LguI) sample of pGE2 to construct a plasmid encoding a mini-CRISPR array expressing a spacer targeting the original SIRV2 genome.
Store the purified pGE2-Spcgp48 sample at −20°C until needed.

Design and order two pairs of primers which will anneal to and amplify the regions of the virus genome located immediately up and downstream from the target gene (deletions) and target site (modifications).
Amplify the left arm of the donor DNA by PCR using one pair of designed primers.
Amplify the right arm of the donor DNA by PCR using the other pair of designed primers.
Perform fusion PCR to combine the left and right arms, generating a full-length donor DNA element.
Include a 5′-overhang of a particular sequence in every primer used for donor DNA assembly.
Set up the first round of PCR reactions according to specified conditions.
Verify the length/purity of the left and right arm PCR fragments by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Purify the PCR fragments of the left and right arm with the GeneJET™ PCR Purification Kit.
Set up the second round of PCR according to the specified tables.
Mix both arms of the donor DNA at equal concentrations in the PCR mixture.
Do not add the two outer primers until after the hold at 4°C.
Complete the first stage of the PCR program without adding the outer primers.
Allow the left and right arms of the donor DNA to denature, mix, and reanneal.
Extend DNA polymerase from the exposed 3′-ends of overlapping sequences.
Calculate the annealing temperature using the salt-adjusted melting temperature of the primers/overlapping sequences with OligoCalc.
Analyze the fusion PCR fragment by agarose gel electrophoresis to verify fusion of left and right arms.
Purify the full-length donor DNA element with the GeneJET™ PCR Purification Kit.
Digest the donor DNA element using FD PaeI/XhoI.
Clone the digested donor DNA element into the linearized (FD PaeI/XhoI) and dephosphorylated (Fast AP) sample of pGE2-Spcgp48.
Use Escherichia coli DH5α for cloning work and purifying plasmids at high yields.
Send a sample of purified pSIRV2Mgp48his for sequencing at an external partner.
Store the purified pSIRV2Mgp48his at −20°C until needed.
Cast a 0.7% gelrite/SCV plate.
Preheat 5 mL of 2×SCV medium in a glass tube.
Preheat 5 mL of 0.4% gelrite in another glass tube.
Transfer 950 μL of 1× medium salts solution to a microcentrifuge tube.
Preheat the microcentrifuge tube to 78°C on a heat block next to the Gene Pulser Xcell™ electroporation system.
Unpack the Gene Pulser/MicroPulser electroporation cuvettes (0.1 cm gap) and place them within reach near the Gene Pulser Xcell™ electroporation system.
Retrieve microcentrifuge tubes containing 50 μL aliquots of electrocompetent S. islandicus LAL14/1 Δarrays cells from the −80°C freezer.
Thaw the cells on ice for approximately 5 minutes.
Transfer 1 μL of a purified plasmid sample (300–500 ng) to the 50 μL aliquot of cells.
Gently flick the microcentrifuge tube to ensure proper mixing.
Prepare a negative control mixture by transferring milliQ-H2O instead of the plasmid DNA to another aliquot of cells.
Transfer the cell-plasmid mixture to a Gene Pulser/MicroPulser electroporation cuvette (0.1 cm gap).
Place the brown cap back on the cuvette and tap it on the desk a few times to collect the mixture in the bottom of the gap.
Load the cuvette into the shockpod of the GenePulser Xcell™ electroporation system.
Pulse the mixture using the GenePulser Xcell™ electroporation system.
Immediately after electroporation, transfer approximately 600 μL of preheated medium salts solution to the cuvette.
Mix briefly by pipetting up and down in the cuvette.
Transfer the cells and medium back into the microcentrifuge tube on the heat block set to 78°C.
Incubate for 30 min at 78°C.
Place the 0.7% gelrite/SCV plates in a 78°C incubator 10 minutes before the end of incubation.
Add 100 μL of electroporated cell suspension into 5 mL preheated 2×SCV medium.
Mix thoroughly with preheated 0.4% gelrite.
Distribute this mixture onto the preheated 0.7% gelrite/SCV plate gently.
Incubate plates for 7–10 days at 78°C in sealed plastic bags inside an air-tight container.
Reconstitute colonies of Sulfolobus transformed with plasmid after 10 days of incubation at 78°C.
Use milliQ-H2O instead of plasmid as a negative control to identify false positives.
Inoculate, resuspend, and spot transformants onto a new Gelrite/SCV plate for further incubation at 78°C for 3–5 days.
Test spots showing growth by PCR using Seq-F and Seq-R primers that anneal to the backbone of pGE2.
Perform PCR with milliQ-H2O as negative control instead of cells.
Resuspend cell suspension from a spot onto a fresh 0.7% gelrite/SCV plate.
In case of growth, scrape Sulfolobus cells from the spot and resuspend in 20 μL milliQ-H2O.
Dilute the resuspension 50-fold with milliQ-H2O.
Perform PCR to confirm presence of plasmid pSIRV2Mgp48his using Seq-F and Seq-R primers.
Transfer positive spots into 20 mL of 1× SCV medium for incubation at 78°C for 1–2 days.
Subculture transformants at an OD600 of 0.05.
Incubate the culture for 36 hours or until the OD600 reaches ≅ 0.6–0.7.
Centrifuge 10 mL of the culture at 6,300 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 670 μL of 1× medium salts solution.
Add 200 μL of sterile 87% (v/v) glycerol to the resuspended pellet.
Store the glycerol stocks at -80°C.
Culture plasmid-free Δarrays infected with the virus sample at an MOI around 0.1.
Culture uninfected Δarrays/pSIRV2Mgp48his using a similar volume of sterile 1× medium salts solution instead of the virus sample.
Incubate both cultures for two days while regularly monitoring the OD600.
Take out 1-mL samples from each culture around 24 and 48 hpi.
Store the taken-out samples at room temperature.
Centrifuge collected samples at 10,000 × g for 6 minutes.
Transfer supernatant into new microcentrifuge tubes.
Analyze virus samples by PCR using a primer specific to the donor DNA and another primer annealing to the flanking region in the virus genome.
Repeat the genome editing protocol from step 33 if the band corresponding to the mutant virus is absent or faint.
Propagate an aliquot of the latest virus sample for two additional days in a fresh culture of Δarrays/pSIRV2Mgp48his upon repeat confirmation.
Employ supernatants containing positive virus mutants in a plaque assay following protocol described in step 20.
Using the 1000-μL pipette, pick 10–20 individual plaques from the 0.7% Gelzan CM/SCVU plates.
Inoculate each plaque into 20 μL of 1× medium salts solution.
Resuspend the plaques thoroughly by pipetting up and down a few times.
Repeat the PCR using individual, resuspended plaques as template.
Analyze the amplicons by agarose gel electrophoresis to identify plaques with the desired mutant genotype.
Send the amplified genomic fragments for sequencing at an external service.
Align the mutant virus sequence with the reference genome using pairwise sequence alignment tools (BLAST) to confirm accuracy.
Inoculate the Δarrays/pSIRV2Mgp48his strain from the -80°C glycerol stock into 30 mL fresh SCV medium in an Erlenmeyer flask.
Allow the culture to incubate for two days at 78°C and 150 rpm.
Dilute the culture with fresh SCV medium to a final volume of 1 liter once the 30-mL culture has reached OD600 ≅ 0.8–1.0.
Measure the initial OD600 (should be around 0.025) and allow the 1-liter culture to incubate until OD600 ≅ 0.1.
Dilute the latest SIRV2Mgp48his sample 10-fold in 1× medium salts solution.
Transfer 300 μL of the diluted sample into a 1-liter Δarrays/pSIRV2Mgp48his culture to start virus propagation.
Incubate the host-virus suspension for 36 hours, monitoring OD600 regularly every 12 hours.
If the OD600 exceeds 0.4 at 36 hpi, repeat the procedure with a fresh 1-liter host suspension and a less diluted virus sample.
Centrifuge the 1-liter culture at 10,000 × g for 6 minutes to isolate SIRV2Mgp48his virus particles.
Transfer the supernatant into a new flask after centrifugation.
Perform a plaque assay to determine the virus titer in the infected culture supernatant, following previous instructions.
Inoculate the S. islandicus LAL14/1 ΔCas6(I-D) host strain from its −80°C glycerol stock into an Erlenmeyer flask filled with 20 mL fresh SCV(U) medium.
Inoculate the S. islandicus LAL14/1 ΔCas6(I-D)/pCmr6α-HA host strain from its −80°C glycerol stock into an Erlenmeyer flask filled with 20 mL fresh SCV medium.
Allow both cultures to incubate for two days.
Transfer each 20-mL culture into fresh, pre-heated medium to a final volume of 120 mL.
Incubate the cultures for approximately 24 hours.
Split each 120-mL culture in two and transfer each half into fresh, pre-heated medium to a final volume of 1 liter.
Allow these cultures to incubate for approximately 20 hours.
Transfer 150 mL of each culture into new 2-liter Duran® bottles containing 850 mL fresh, pre-heated medium when the four 1-liter cultures reach an OD600 ≅ 0.4.
Incubate all parallel cultures overnight (approximately 12–14 hours).
Infect each culture with SIRV2Mgp48his sample to achieve MOI = 1.
Incubate infected cultures for 3 hours.
Remove bottles from incubator and allow cultures to cool down to room temperature.
Centrifuge cell cultures at 6,300 × g and 16°C for 10 minutes.
Discard supernatants and weigh the cell pellets.
Resuspend cell pellets in cold lysis buffer (5 mL per gram of pellet) on ice.
Transfer resuspended cell pellets into Falcon tubes.
Store Falcon tubes containing resuspended cells at -80°C until needed.
Sonicate the sample with 30 cycles of 3-s pulses intervened by 3-s pauses.
Homogenize the sample with a French press equilibrated with lysis buffer, performing two rounds.
Sonicate the sample again using the same program as in the first sonication step.
Rinse the sonicator rod with 70% ethanol between individual samples to avoid contamination.
Run 20% ethanol through the French press several times between individual samples and before and after use of the instrument.
Centrifuge lysed cell samples at 16,000 × g and 4°C for 45 min to remove cell debris.
Transfer supernatants to new Falcon tubes.
Repeat centrifugation until precipitates are smaller than a fingernail and supernatants become slightly transparent.
Spin down Ni-NTA agarose resin at 800 × g for 3 min in a swinging-bucket centrifuge.
Discard storage buffer from the resin and resuspend each resin bed in 10 mL of lysis buffer.
Repeat substeps to equilibrate Ni-NTA agarose resin five times or more.
Filter supernatants through sterile, non-pyrogenic hydrophilic filters (0.45 μm).
Mix filtered supernatants with the equilibrated Ni-NTA agarose resins in 50-mL Falcon tubes.
Incubate mixtures overnight at 4°C on a rotary wheel set to 10 rpm.
Spin the protein-bound Ni-NTA resins at 800 × g for 3 min in a swinging-bucket centrifuge.
Discard the supernatants and wash the protein-bound Ni-NTA resins.
Add 10 mL of lysis buffer to each resin bed and incubate for 5 min on the rotary wheel set to 10 rpm.
Spin down the agarose resins at 800 × g for 3 min in a swinging-bucket centrifuge and remove the supernatant.
Repeat substeps washing and spinning five times.
After the last centrifugation, resuspend the resin beds in 0.8–1.0 mL lysis buffer each and transfer to microcentrifuge tubes.
Spin down the microcentrifuge tubes at 800 × g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Add an equal volume of elution buffer to the protein-bound Ni-NTA agarose resin beds and incubate the tubes for 5 min on a rotary wheel set to 10 rpm.
Spin down the microcentrifuge tube with the elution mixture at 800 × g for 3 min and transfer the supernatant to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Refill the microcentrifuge with a fresh bed volume of elution buffer.
Repeat substeps eluting and spinning five times.
Combine the collected eluates into one volume.
Concentrate proteins via spin filtering using a Pierce™ Protein Concentrator PES (10K MWCO).
Centrifuge protein solutions at 10,000 × g for rounds of 4 minutes until only 100 μL is left in each spin column.
Transfer the retentates into new microcentrifuge tubes and store them at 4°C until needed.
Mix 15 μL of each concentrated protein sample with 5 μL of 4× SDS loading buffer.
Incubate the mixture for 5 minutes on a heat block set to 95°C.
Collect the mixtures at the bottom of the microcentrifuge tube by a brief spin down.
Separate the samples on a 12% SDS-PAGE gel at 16 mA for up to 2 hours with the voltage set to a maximum of 120 V.
Remove the gel from the chamber and stain it for 1 hour with a Coomassie Brilliant Blue (R-250)-based staining solution.
Destain the gels repeatedly in destaining solution until protein bands can be distinguished clearly from the background.
Resolve the concentrated protein samples on another 12% SDS-PAGE gel without staining and destaining the gel after the run.
Wash the separation gel with distilled H2O.
Soak blotting papers and Nitrocellulose membrane in transfer buffer.
Arrange the transfer assembly top-to-bottom: cathode, blotting paper, SDS-polyacrylamide gel, nitrocellulose membrane, blotting paper, anode.
Remove any air bubbles during assembly by gently rolling a cylindrical object over the setup before placing it between the cathode and anode.
Connect the transfer assembly to the power source and perform protein transfer at 70 mA for 75 minutes.
Set voltage to any value >20 V to prevent voltage from being the limiting factor during transfer.
Carefully separate the nitrocellulose membrane from the gel and blotting papers once the transfer is complete.
Incubate the membrane in wash buffer (WB) for 2 minutes.
Dissolve 1.5 grams of skim milk in WB to prepare blocking buffer.
Replace WB with 30 mL of blocking buffer and incubate at RT on a shaking platform for 30 minutes.
Store the membrane soaked in the blocking buffer overnight at 4°C if needed (approx. 14 hours).
Wash the nitrocellulose membrane three times with WB for 3 minutes each at RT on a shaking platform.
Allow the membrane to incubate at RT for 30 minutes on a shaking platform before washing step if stored overnight at 4°C.
Prepare primary antibody solution by mixing “HA Tag Monoclonal Antibody (2–2.2.14)” and WB at 1:10000 final ratio.
Discard the WB and incubate the membrane in the primary antibody solution for 1–4 hours at RT on a shaking platform.
Prepare the secondary antibody solution by mixing Goat anti-Mouse IgG (H+L) Secondary Antibody with WB at a 1:3000 v/v final ratio.
Discard the WB and incubate the membrane in the secondary antibody solution for 1 h at RT on a shaking platform.
Mix equal volumes of Stable Peroxide Solution and Luminol/Enhancer Solution from the SuperSignalTM West Pico PLUS Chemiluminescent Substrate Kit to form the substrate mixture.
Remove as much WB as possible without drying the membrane and transfer the Nitrocellulose membrane into a dry container.
Spread the substrate mixture uniformly across the membrane and incubate for 2–3 min.
Place the membrane between two transparent plastic sheets, remove any air bubbles, and bind it within a Kodak BioMax Cassette.
In a darkroom, place an X-ray film directly on top of the plastic-wrapped membrane.
Develop the film using the developer and fixer solutions after 30–60 s.
